predecessors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
predecessors.text: the Rif coast and the Nekor valley, granted to Salih I ibn Mansur by the Caliphate

successors.name: Almoravid dynasty
successors.text: the Rif around the Nekor river, taken by Yusuf ibn Tashfin 'during his conquest of the Rif'

ledger.x: 710: Salih I ibn Mansur founds the emirate of Nekor in the Rif.
750: the Umayyad overlord falls and the emirate stands alone.
760: the seat moves from Temsamane to Nekor.
By 931: Nekor a client of Cordoba.
The page gives no end to the fighting: the emirate is back under its Salihid line (emirs 947-970 in the infobox).
The page does not say when the Cordoban vassalage ended; 934 is the next dated event ('Fatimid troops sacked the city twice, in 917 and in 934').
About 1015: the Salihid line gives way to Ya'la ibn al-Fatuh of the Azdaja tribe.
1081: the emirate of Nekor ends with the destruction of its city.

wars.name: Viking raid on Nekor (859)
wars.outcome: The Vikings, after Seville and Algeciras, 'plundered the city for eight days' and defeated a force that tried to stop them; no change of land.

wars.name: Fatimid sacks of Nekor
wars.outcome: Fatimid troops sacked the city in 917 and again in 934; the emirate survived.

wars.name: Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya's campaign against Nekor
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman III occupies Melilla (927); Musa defeats the Umayyad vassal al-Mu'ayyad and sacks and burns Nekor (931).

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the Rif
wars.outcome: Yusuf ibn Tashfin destroys Nekor in 1080-1081 'for the fourth and last time' during his conquest of the Rif.

certainty.note: A Rif tribal emirate with no surveyed or treaty frontier on any page opened; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation of the Nekor valley and coast.
